title: Editing Summarized Content
use_cases: Use when minor typos need correction within already archived story segments
Implement when significant plot changes require synchronization with AI memory
Configure when starting major revisions that invalidate previous plot summaries
Use when maintaining strict logical consistency for AI-assisted writing
content:
If you edit parts of your story that have already been summarized, those summaries become outdated.

AI Story Stream will warn you when you try to edit summarized sections and give you three options:

1. Continue Anyway – Edit the content, but know that summaries are now inaccurate
2. Reset Summaries – Clear all summaries so you can edit freely, then re-summarize later
3. Cancel Edit – Keep your summaries intact and don't make changes

For minor edits (fixing typos, tweaking a sentence), you can continue without worry. For major revisions like rewriting entire chapters or changing plot points, it's best to reset summaries and regenerate them after you're done.

Why this matters: if your summaries say "Marcus trusted Elena completely" but you've edited the scene to make him suspicious of her, the AI will get conflicting information. Accurate summaries mean accurate story continuity.
